_README: CORS for direct browser -> S3 uploads (product images) and invoice downloads.
REQUIRED because the browser uploads product images straight to S3 using a
presigned PUT URL. A presigned URL authorises the HTTP request, but the
browser still enforces CORS on the RESPONSE - without this rule the upload
succeeds server-side and the page then fails to read the result.
ALLOWED_ORIGINS MUST NOT BE "*". A wildcard is rejected for requests that
carry credentials, and combined with presigned URLs it would let any site
cause authenticated uploads against this bucket.
ALLOWED_METHODS is PUT and GET only: the browser never needs POST or DELETE.
AllowedHeaders must include the headers the app signs into the presigned
request. Content-Type is signed (S3Service signs ContentType), so omitting it
here produces SignatureDoesNotMatch even though the URL is valid.
ExposeHeaders must include ETag if the client ever needs it after upload.
ALLOWED_ORIGINS below MUST match FRONTEND_URL and ADMIN_FRONTEND_URL in
infra/ecs-task-definition.json exactly. This rule is what lets the ADMIN
portal upload product images: it is the admin origin, not the storefront
origin, that calls generatePresignedUploadUrl. Omitting admin.vedhicfoods.com
here makes image upload fail in the browser while succeeding server-side —
the PUT returns 200 and the page still cannot read the response.
These are plain hostnames, not origins with a scheme: S3 AllowedOrigins
rejects a value containing "https://" and the whole put-bucket-cors call
fails with MalformedXML.
